Reviewing clips in the BirdNET GUI

Source: vignettes/articles/reviewing-in-the-gui.Rmd
reviewing-in-the-gui.Rmd

The manual review of stage 1 happens outside R, in the Review tab of the BirdNET-Analyzer GUI. This article walks through that review, from the folder of clips written by cut_clips() to the Positive and Negative folders that classify_review() reads back. The screenshots were taken with GUI version 2.4.0 (model V2.4) on Windows, on clips of the FrogNet project; the layout may differ in other versions. The GUI documentation describes how to install and launch it, and states that the Review tab implements the workflow of Wood & Kahl (2024).

The folder of clips

extract_validation_clips() (or cut_clips()) writes one folder per species under clips/, each with the clips to review. The name of a clip starts with its confidence score and its rank, followed by the name of the source recording and the start and end of the clip:

The clips of one species, ready for review.

The GUI reads the species from the names of these subfolders.

Choosing the species

In the Review tab, Select input directory points the GUI to the clips folder. The Species list then shows one entry per subfolder, and the counters show the clips still to review (Todo) and those already classified as Positive or Negative:

The Review tab with the list of species.

Reviewing a clip

Each clip is shown as a spectrogram, with an audio player (with Autoplay, the clip plays as soon as it opens). The name of the clip, with its score, is shown above the waveform. Positive and Negative classify the clip and move to the next one; Undo reverses the last decision and Skip moves on without classifying:

Reviewing a clip. The score of this clip (0.992) is the first field of its name.

Review the clip by listening to it, not only by its score: the score is what the review is meant to check. For the random designs of vignette("sampling-designs"), the order in which the clips are reviewed does not matter, but every clip of a drawn occasion must be reviewed (see vignette("crywolf-integration")).

The regression panel

Once clips have been classified, the Regression panel shows a logistic regression of the verdicts on the score for the selected species, with the scores at which the predicted probability of a true detection reaches 0.85, 0.90, 0.95 and 0.99:

The Review tab after the review of one species: 72 positive and 7 negative clips, and the fitted curve.

This curve is a quick check during the review. It is fitted to one species at a time, pooling every site, on the clips reviewed so far. The calibration of stage 2 (calibrate(), vignette("calibration")) fits the species and sites together, lets the curve differ among them, compares the candidate models by cross-validation and, with engine = "brms", carries the uncertainty of the curve. Use the GUI curve to follow the review, and the calibration of stage 2 for the analyses.

The result: Positive and Negative folders

The GUI moves each classified clip into a Positive or a Negative subfolder of the species folder:

The species folder after the review.

This is the structure that classify_review() and post_validation() read. The verdict of each clip comes from the name of the subfolder in which it is found, matched by the regular expressions positive_pattern ("positiv" by default) and negative_pattern ("negativ"), case insensitive. A clip left in the species folder, outside Positive and Negative (for instance when the review was interrupted), is counted as not_reviewed; a clip of the manifest not found at all, as clip_missing.

library(sheepdog)
res <- post_validation(review_dir    = "C:/clips",
                       manifest_path = "C:/validation/clip_manifest.csv",
                       output_dir    = "C:/validation/results")

The interface in Portuguese

The GUI can be switched to Portuguese in its settings (the translation is by Larissa Sugai, according to the GUI documentation). The buttons become Positivo, Negativo, Desfazer and Pular, and the regression panel, Regressão:

The Review tab in Portuguese.
The list of species in Portuguese.
Reviewing a clip in Portuguese.

With the interface in Portuguese, the GUI names the result folders positivo and negativo instead of Positive and Negative. The default patterns of classify_review() ("positiv", "negativ", case insensitive) match both, so the review can be read back in either language, and clips reviewed partly in each language end up in the right verdict. The regression panel of a species with more false positives looks different: here the curve reaches 0.85 only at a score of 0.81, and 0.90 at 0.93, and the higher probabilities are not reached within the range of scores:

The regression panel for a species with more false positives.

Species like this are those that cell_status() flags as unreliable at p_min = 0.95 (see vignette("community-matrices")).

Several reviewers

When the clips are split among reviewers, each reviewer reviews their own copy of the folder tree in the GUI. assign_reviewers() splits the clips (with a fraction reviewed twice), split_by_reviewer() copies them, and after the review reviewer_agreement() and consensus_verdicts() measure the agreement and combine the verdicts:

man <- assign_reviewers(read.csv("C:/validation/clip_manifest.csv"),
                        reviewers = c("ana", "bia", "caio"), overlap = 0.1)
split_by_reviewer(man, clips_dir = "C:/validation/clips",
                  output_dir = "C:/review")

# after each reviewer has reviewed C:/review/<reviewer> in the GUI
reviews <- lapply(c(ana = "ana", bia = "bia", caio = "caio"), function(r)
  classify_review(man, file.path("C:/review", r)))
reviewer_agreement(reviews)
validation <- consensus_verdicts(reviews)

Clips with conflicting verdicts get verdict = "disagreement" and are left out of the precision and the calibration until a consensus review settles them.

References

Wood, C. M., & Kahl, S. (2024). Guidelines for appropriate use of BirdNET scores and other detector outputs. Journal of Ornithology, 165, 777–782. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10336-024-02144-5
